title: Candy Crush
statement:
You get an `m x n` grid `board` of integers for a simple candy-matching game. A positive value is a candy of that type and `0` is an empty cell. Repeat the following until nothing changes, then return the final board:

1. **Crush.** Find every horizontal or vertical line of three or more consecutive cells holding the same candy type. All candies on any such line disappear at the same moment (their cells become `0`). A candy can belong to a horizontal and a vertical line at once.
2. **Drop.** In every column, candies above empty cells fall straight down until they rest on the bottom row or on another candy. The column keeps its order, and the cells left at the top stay `0` (no new candies appear).
3. If step 1 crushed nothing, the board is stable: stop and return it. Otherwise, go back to step 1, since falling candies may have formed new lines.

You may change `board` in place; return the stable board.
constraints: 1 <= board[i][j] <= 2000 (the initial board has no empty cells)
notes:
## Intuition

This is a pure simulation: do exactly what the rules say, round after round, until a round crushes nothing. The only subtle part is the word "simultaneously". A candy can sit on a horizontal and a vertical line at once (a T or L shape), so a cell must not be emptied while other lines are still being looked for. Instead, mark it by making its value negative: `Math.abs` still shows its type to the other scans, and the sign says "crush me". Gravity is then a per-column compaction of the positive values toward the bottom.

## Approach

1. Set `stable = false` and loop until a round leaves it `true`.
2. Horizontal scan: for every window of three cells `(r, c)`, `(r, c + 1)`, `(r, c + 2)` whose absolute values are equal and non-zero, negate all three and set `stable = false`. Longer lines are covered by overlapping windows.
3. Vertical scan: the same with windows going down a column.
4. Drop: in each column, walk from the bottom with a `write` pointer; copy every positive value to `board[write][c]` and move `write` up. Fill the cells above `write` with `0`. Negative (crushed) and empty cells are skipped.
5. When a round marks nothing, return `board`.

## Example 1, step by step

Round 1 finds three lines: the four 1s in column 1 (rows 6 to 9), the three 2s in column 2 (rows 6 to 8) and the three 2s in row 8 (columns 2 to 4). The cell `(8, 2)` is on two of them. After the drop, new lines have formed: four 5s in row 4, three 3s in row 5, five 1s in row 8 and four 4s in row 9. Round 2 crushes all of them at once and the rest falls. Round 3 marks nothing, so the loop ends with the expected board, whose top three rows are empty.

## Complexity

- Time: O((m·n)²) in the worst case: a round costs O(m·n), and every round except the last removes at least three candies, so there are at most m·n/3 + 1 rounds. Real boards settle in far fewer.
- Space: O(1) extra: marks and drops happen in place.

## Pitfalls

- Setting cells to `0` as soon as a line is found breaks crossing lines; in Test 5 the vertical line of 1s would lose its top cell. Mark first, clear later.
- Skip value `0`: three empty cells in a row are not a line.
- Compare absolute values, or a marked candy stops matching its neighbours.
- One crush-and-drop is not enough: falling candies can form new lines, so repeat until stable.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | board height and width |
| `stable` | stays `true` only if a whole round finds no line |
| `r`, `c` | the cell where a three-cell window starts |
| `value` | the candy type at `(r, c)`, ignoring a crush mark |
| `write` | the lowest cell in the column still waiting for a falling candy |

narration.6: Keep running rounds until one of them crushes nothing.
narration.7: Assume this round finds no line until a scan proves otherwise.
narration.9: Slide a window of three cells along each row.
narration.10: Read the candy type, ignoring a minus sign left by an earlier mark.
narration.11: Three equal, non-empty candies side by side form a line.
narration.12: Mark all three by negating them; their type stays readable for the other scans.
narration.13: Something was crushed, so another round will be needed.
narration.17: Now slide a window of three cells down each column.
narration.20: Three equal, non-empty candies stacked vertically form a line.
narration.21: Mark them too; a cell may already be marked by a row line.
narration.26: Apply gravity one column at a time.
narration.27: The next candy that survives will land at the bottom-most free cell.
narration.28: Walk the column from the bottom up.
narration.29: Only unmarked candies survive; marked and empty cells are skipped.
narration.30: Move the surviving candy down to its resting cell.
narration.31: The next survivor lands one cell higher.
narration.34: Everything above the last survivor is empty...
narration.40: A full round found no line: the board is stable.
